messages.content: "In a game of basketball, a player has a 60% chance of making any given shot. In a series of 10 shots, what is the probability that the player makes exactly 7 shots? Also, in another series of 15 shots, what is the probability that the player makes exactly 10 shots? Finally, in a series of 20 shots, what is the probability that the player makes exactly 15 shots?"

function.name: calculate_binomial_probability
function.description: Calculates the binomial probability given the number of trials, successes and the probability of success on an individual trial. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

number_of_successes.description: The desired number of successful outcomes.

probability_of_success.description: The probability of a successful outcome on any given trial. This is a float type value.

message.content:
**Binomial set‑up**

The player takes independent shots where  

\[
P(\text{make}) = p = 0.60,\qquad  
P(\text{miss}) = q = 1-p = 0.40 .
\]

If he shoots \(n\) times, the probability of getting **exactly** \(k\) made baskets is

\[
\boxed{\displaystyle 
P_{n}(k)= \binom{n}{k}\,p^{\,k}\,q^{\,n-k}}
\]

---

### 1. 10 shots – exactly 7 made

\[
\begin{aligned}
P_{10}(7)
&=\binom{10}{7}(0.6)^7(0.4)^3\\[4pt]
&=120\times0.6^7\times0.4^3 \\[4pt]
&\approx 120\times0.0279936\times0.064\\[4pt]
&\approx 0.21499 .
\end{aligned}
\]

> **About 21.5 %** of the time the player will hit exactly seven of ten shots.

---

### 2. 15 shots – exactly 10 made

\[
\begin{aligned}
P_{15}(10)
&=\binom{15}{10}(0.6)^{10}(0.4)^5\\[4pt]
&=3003\times0.6^{10}\times0.4^5\\[4pt]
&\approx 3003\times0.0060472\times0.01024\\[4pt]
&\approx 0.18596 .
\end{aligned}
\]

> **Approximately 18.6 %** of the time the player will make exactly ten of fifteen shots.

---

### 3. 20 shots – exactly 15 made

\[
\begin{aligned}
P_{20}(15)
&=\binom{20}{15}(0.6)^{15}(0.4)^5\\[4pt]
&=15504\times0.6^{15}\times0.4^5\\[4pt]
&\approx 15504\times0.0004703\times0.01024\\[4pt]
&\approx 0.07466 .
\end{aligned}
\]

> **Around 7.5 %** of the time the player will score exactly fifteen of twenty attempts.

---

#### Quick sanity checks

| Shots | Expected #made (\(np\)) | Std dev (\(\sqrt{npq}\)) |
|-------|------------------------|--------------------------|
| 10    | 6                      | 1.55                     |
| 15    | 9                      | 1.90                     |
| 20    | 12                     | 2.19                     |

The most likely counts cluster close to the expectation; hitting far beyond it becomes progressively rarer—hence the drop from ~21 % down to ~7 %.

Feel free to plug the parameters into any calculator or spreadsheet if you’d like to confirm the decimals yourself!
